subject: Workplace Skills
title: Why Leaders Struggle to Delegate
description: A quick win: understand Why Leaders Struggle to Delegate.

hook.text: A new manager kept doing her old job plus managing. She burned out in four months. She couldn't let go.

buildup.text: Leaders who were strong individual contributors struggle most. Doing the work felt productive; delegating feels risky.

discovery.text: Delegation isn't about offloading work. It's about multiplying output through others while freeing yourself.

twist.text: The work quality might dip initially when delegated. That temporary dip is the investment cost of growing your team.

climax.text: Ask: 'Is this task that only I can do?' If not, delegate it. Protect your time for what only you can contribute.

punchline.text: Only do what only you can do. Delegate the rest.

quiz.question: Why do former top individual contributors often struggle with delegation?
options: They don't trust their team's technical skills
Doing the work felt productive while delegating feels risky
Companies don't train new managers on delegation
